## Purpose
Most `mustard-rt run` diagnostics and maintenance commands under `doctor/`, `maint/`, `pipeline/`, and `review/` end in a `*Report` struct: a serializable, deterministic bundle carrying the verdict plus enough evidence to act on it. `BootstrapReport`, `CapabilityDriftReport`, `MaintDepsReport`, `MaintValidateReport` all follow the same shape — an outer struct with `ok`/`overall` plus a `Vec` of per-item records. This mold teaches the fields and derives a new Report struct needs so it composes with the same fail-open, byte-stable rendering the rest of the CLI relies on.

## Convention
Folder: apps/rt/src/commands/doctor/**, apps/rt/src/commands/maint/**, apps/rt/src/commands/pipeline/**, apps/rt/src/commands/review/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 25
The three exemplars read (`bootstrap_check.rs`, `capability_drift_check.rs`, `doctor.rs`) show a Report struct that derives `Serialize` (or is hand-rendered via `serde_json::json!` in `doctor.rs`'s `CheckResult`/render functions) and carries a boolean summary field (`ok`) first, then counts, then `Vec<Item>` fields for the evidence, sorted deterministically before being returned. A companion `*Finding`/`*Item` struct carries a closed-vocabulary `kind`/`status` tag plus a `detail`/`remedy` string — never free-form prose alone. Every producing function is fail-open: an unreadable input degrades to an empty/ok report, never a panic or `Result::Err`.

## How to apply
A new command under one of these four families that reports on repo/installation health defines its own `<Name>Report` + `<Name>Item`/`<Name>Finding` pair in its own file, following the `ok`-first field order and the sorted-vector convention (`CapabilityDriftReport`'s `drifted.sort_by(...)`). It wires into `doctor.rs`'s dispatch only if it is a doctor check; `maint`/`pipeline`/`review` reports are returned directly from their own `run()` and printed by the caller as pretty JSON.
